head: ai-replay-budget-r2
report:
NO DEFECTS

I found nothing at this head that the author must fix before merge. All four earlier findings are closed: I ran the earlier reviewer's five probe files, copied without changes, against the snapshot's `node_modules`. The 20-minute budget ran out before I finished every path; what I did not reach is listed at the end.

## NOT A DEFECT

**Earlier findings, replayed at this head:**

| Earlier finding | Status | Evidence at this head |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Requests sent after the deadline (`late-wakeup` on seven HTTP providers, Anthropic extended wait, `late-prepare`, `cursor-late-wait`) | Closed | All `probes.test.ts` cases pass. `cursor-late-wait`: 1 request, marked `true`, 803 ms elapsed. The fix asks the budget again just before each send: `fetchWithRetry` holds the failure in `pending` and calls `retryGate(0)`, and each provider checks `replayOf`/`correctionOf` the same way. |
| 2. Server waits bypassed (`over-provider-cap`, `short-header-long-body`, Gemini `alternate-endpoint-hint`) | Closed | Probes pass. Gemini made 1 call, marked `true`, and the error kept `retry-after-ms=30000`. The fix is `longestServerWaitMs` / `longestRetryHint` plus `switchesEndpoint` in `google-gemini-cli.ts`. |
| 3. First resume poll sent even with no budget left | Closed | `resume.test.ts` passes: only the initial POST, 47 ms, marked `true` (the earlier run took 12038 ms). `pollOpenAIResponsesResultForCompletion` now calls `admits(0)` before every poll, the first included. The earlier characterization test `resume always issues its first check even with a refused budget` now fails (expected 1 fetch, got 0). The earlier report predicted exactly this once the fix landed, so it is not a regression. |
| 4. Budget marker set when the provider stopped on its own (`own-correction-ceiling`) | Closed | Both runs (budget 10000 and 100) sent 3 requests and left the marker unset (`null`). `attemptedReasoningEffortFallbacks.has(...)` is now checked before `admitsReplay`. |

**Totals:** `probes.test.ts` 92 pass, 1 fail (the characterization test above). `extra.test.ts` 3/3 pass. `resume.test.ts` 1/1 pass.

**The patch's own tests:** `replay-budget-wire.test.ts` and `empty-completion-retry.test.ts` pass (80/80). `agent-session-held-retry-replay-budget.test.ts` passes (1/1).

**Suspicions I checked and ruled out:**
- **`fetchWithRetry` order:** the gate is asked only after the `maxAttempts`, `shouldRetryResponse` and over-cap checks, so the provider's own last attempt never sets the marker. The abort path and a failed wait both release the held response.
- **Anthropic loop:** every rung that sends again is gated (the `continue` paths at 3219–3592 plus the backoff at 3633). `replayOf` is checked at 2603 before the request is built.
- **OpenAI Responses:** in the fallback loop, refusing the strict-tools rung falls through to the chain-baseline branch, which throws while the refusal is latched. The marker is correct there.
- **Gemini CLI:** a refused empty-stream retry `break`s, then throws "empty response". The endpoint switch that follows is refused by the latched budget, so the result is still an error, not an empty success.
- **Cursor:** all three places that re-enter `streamCursorWithWireMode` (2020, 2073, 2163) pass `replayBudget` along, so a continued request cannot lose the budget.
- **Codex:** `retryDelayMs` is computed with `providerRetryAttempt + 1` before the increment. Without a budget this gives the same wait as before.
- **Bedrock:** both callers of `sendBedrockRequest` were updated to pass the now-required `signal` parameter.
- **Replay-safe wrapper:** each inner attempt gets `budget.remainingMs()` (shared deadline), and the outer wrapper asks `admits(0)` again after its own wait.
- **`HELD_RETRY_REPLAY_BUDGET_MS` in `turn-recovery.ts`:**
  - **Wait threshold:** `sameModelWaitMs < 2000` stops the hold when the wait is 2 s or longer. With the default `retry.baseDelayMs` of 500 ms the hold still applies. A user who sets the base delay to 2000 ms or more loses the hold; the code comment says longer waits should go to the chain, so I treat this as deliberate.
  - **Lifetime:** the held budget is set after the backoff sleep and cleared in `resetForNewPrompt`, `#endCancelledRetry`, and when the next request consumes it.
- **`replayBudgetExhausted` in coding-agent:** nothing there reads it. The fallback chain still walks on the second failure because `#retryAttempt !== 1`, so this is not a request that gets dropped.

**Noticed but not asserted:** in `fetch-retry.ts`, if `prepareInit` throws while a 5xx/429 response is held in `pending`, that response's body is never cancelled. I did not reproduce this or measure any impact.

**Not reached in the time:** the h2-client cleanup when Cursor's send-time check throws, and whether any side request (for example compaction) goes through `primaryStreamFn` before the held retry and consumes the held budget first.
